content.comment_body: I've developed a program to control an industrial oven and it's working well so far, thanks to the helpful responses I've received. I do have a couple of questions and would appreciate any guidance. 1) I'm operating two fans—an input fan and an exhaust fan—using pressure switches to verify operation. I need to confirm both the open and closed status of these switches. At startup, the system checks that the pressure switches are open, then starts the fans, and looks for the switches to close. If all is correct, the process continues. However, if a switch opens during operation, the system should stop. I'm unsure how to implement this logic. 2) I'm using two inputs as push buttons to activate functions and change menus. Currently, pressing one button starts the sequence, but it's possible to press the second button as well. I want to interlock these inputs so that if one is pressed, the other cannot be activated. I'm not sure how to accomplish this. Thanks in advance.

analysis.insight_summary: The user has successfully set up core automation but faces challenges with specific control logic for pressure switches and input interlocking in managing an industrial oven. The difficulties highlight the need for clearer instructions or built-in examples for handling these scenarios within the programming environment.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for straightforward, step-by-step support or sample solutions for implementing pressure switch validation and robust input interlocking mechanisms in their automation setup.
